title: Session crediting with smoothed IO minimums and SQ gating
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Hypothesis: Introducing a session-aware crediting model with a short rolling smoothing window will improve revenue predictability for customers while reducing billing disputes and friction during streaming-heavy workloads. We will pair this with an enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) gating flow for customers requesting custom minimums or committed credits. This ticket scopes the experiment design, instrumentation, legal gating, and rollout plan for three pricing arms (baseline, smoothed soft minimum, commit-credit option behind SQ).
experiment_design: Three-arm randomized experiment: A) Baseline - existing per-token IO metering (control). B) Smoothed Soft-Min - per-session soft minimum computed over a 24-hour rolling window with grace credits applied for the first 3 sessions after onboarding. C) Commit Credit - customers can opt into a reserved commit that converts a portion of ingress to pre-paid credits; access to this arm requires SQ approval and contract amendment. Randomize at customer-account level; stratify by 90-day spend decile and region.
metrics_primary: Net revenue per active account (7d running)
Rate of billing disputes (support tickets per 10k sessions)
Conversion rate to paid plan for trial customers
metrics_secondary: Churn rate at 30d for customers impacted by minimums
acceptance_criteria: Statistically significant >3% uplift in revenue per active account without >2% increase in churn
<15% of impacted customers file a dispute within 14 days
SQ gating flow completed and legal sign-off available for commit-credit pilot
telemetry_and_instrumentation: New dimension: session_smoothing_window (24h/72h variants in A/B internal test)
SQL cohort queries: active_accounts_7d, disputed_sessions_14d, commit_optins_by_region
rollout_plan: 1) Internal shadow roll for 2 weeks to validate billing pipeline and grace-credit logic. 2) Open randomized rollout at 5% accounts (stratified) for 30 days. 3) Expand to 25% if safety metrics pass, and enable SQ gating for manual sales requests. 4) If >3% lift and dispute rates acceptable, propose release as beta product with opt-in commit contracts for enterprise customers.
rollback_criteria: >2% point increase in 30d churn, >20% rise in billing disputes, or critical billing pipeline errors >1/hr for 3 consecutive hours.
legal_and_sq_requirements: Create SQ checklist to validate eligibility for commit-credit: data residency, audit logs, KMS integration, contract duration >=6 months
Draft contract amendment template with finance and legal for pre-paid credits
Security review required before enabling commit-credit for any account
operational_tasks: Billing engine: implement session smoothing aggregator and grace-credit ledger
Console: surface projected monthly cost w/soft-min preview in UI
Support playbook: standardized responses and refund policy for grace-credit disputes
QA: end-to-end tests for streaming edge-cases and partial-session reconnection

notes: We should test both 24h and 72h smoothing windows in a small internal A/A test before exposing to customers.
Grace-credit behavior: first 3 sessions after onboarding should not be charged toward minimum to reduce early churn risk.
Sales teams must route commit requests through legal intake to enforce SQ gating; automation ticket pending ENG-50211.
